analysis.title: BoJ Monetary Policy Meeting Preview: Re-examining risk balance between growth and prices
key_insights: The BoJ is widely expected to hold its policy rate at 1.25% at next week's meeting. Market pricing for a second consecutive hike in October peaked near 40% and has since receded.
Citi expects hawkish Board member Hajime Takata to submit another rate hike proposal, which would not be a surprise. Citi still forecasts the next hike in December.
Citi's base case is quarterly hikes through mid-next year (three further hikes) with a terminal rate of 2%.

The Outlook Report could raise next fiscal year's inflation forecast, because oil price changes pass through to Japanese CPI with a lag of about six to twelve months under the fuel cost adjustment mechanism.
Core CPI has been below 2% for eight consecutive months this year and was 1.7% y/y in August. Citi expects September core CPI, due Friday, to be back above 2%.

The BoJ's description of underlying inflation as 'approaching 2%' could advance to something like 'at broadly 2%'. Citi thinks declaring the target 'achieved' would still be premature, and the assessment that financial conditions remain accommodative is unlikely to change.

Market developments could slow the hike pace: the correction in AI-related stocks and spillover from rising French yields (OATs). Ueda said in September he wants to avoid hikes fast enough to trigger a significant asset price correction.
Citi expects the Fed to hike in December. If the BoJ fails to hike in December, renewed yen weakness could resurface.
Corporate goods prices and the Tankan price indicators suggest price increases are leveling off, so there is little evidence supporting consecutive hikes.

Japan Rates: hike pricing looks fair and range-bound trading is likely. Citi is neutral on duration. The 15y and 20y sectors are favored for bullish delta views, and 5y-10y is a candidate for shorts, though it tends to outperform in risk-off.
10y JGB yields have eased back from a temporary peak above 3%. Super-long demand is strong after a very strong 20y auction on October 20. Citi expects some profit-taking before year-end.

Japan FX: Citi expects USDJPY in a ¥155-160 range near term. The Japanese MoF is turning more hawkish, and Citi expects JPY-buying intervention if USDJPY tops ¥160, aiming to push it below ¥155 or near ¥150.

The MoF and BoJ conducted rate checks after the September 18 meeting with USDJPY near ¥158, well below the ~¥164 level of the end-July intervention. US pressure has shifted from preventing JPY depreciation to promoting appreciation.
Citi expects Japanese intervention if EURJPY tops ¥180 and a second US EURJPY intervention if it rises above ¥182. The US intervened on July 31, and EURJPY has fallen from about ¥185 to about ¥177.

The second Takaichi Cabinet is moving away from its reflationary stance. Minister Kiuchi said 'the stage of reflationary policy has ended'. Whether Kiuchi keeps attending BoJ meetings is a point of focus.
Board member Asada may keep voting against hikes, but Ayano Sato may start voting in favor.

Japan Equities: Citi sees the BoJ meeting as a non-event for stocks. TOPIX has been range-bound between 3,900 and 4,200 since July, with fundamental factors a major negative in Jul-Sep. Citi expects them to recover into year-end as the yield curve flattens and Middle East supply concerns recede.
Citi expects strong July-September Japanese earnings with many positive surprises, after a positive September Tankan surprise in most sectors.

sector_views.rationale: Citi expects fundamentals (earnings revisions, EPS growth) to regain importance into year-end, with strong Jul-Sep earnings and upward guidance revisions supportive.
Hike pricing looks fair and range-bound trading is likely. 15y-20y favored for bullish views, 5y-10y a candidate for shorts.

earnings_insights: Citi expects Japanese July-September earnings to be generally strong with many positive surprises, given the positive September Tankan business sentiment surprise. Upward guidance revisions predominating would be supportive for Japan equities.

Citi forecasts quarterly hikes through mid-next year, with the next in December.
Below 2% for eight consecutive months because of policy-related factors.

risk_factors: Deepening equity correction, particularly in AI-related stocks, could slow the BoJ hike pace.
Spillover from rising French yields could tighten global financial conditions and delay Fed and ECB hikes.
A worsening Middle East situation could cause stagflation-like headwinds via higher commodity prices and bearish bonds.
A BoJ failure to hike in December could bring renewed yen weakness.
Uncertainty about the path beyond December is increasing.
Heavy net JGB supply and possible foreign unwinds of super-long positions.
charts_described: Figure 2 plots Citi's policy rate forecast against OIS market pricing as of October 21.
Figure 21 shows factor returns since July in Japanese equities, with momentum, P/E and EPS revision factors mostly negative.
vol_and_positioning: CitiFX position indices show little recent bias among leveraged investors and only a minor buildup of USD longs and JPY shorts among real money investors, so position adjustments are not expected to move FX much.
OIS short covering followed strong auction results, AI boom concerns and OAT turmoil.
Foreign investors made significant net purchases of super-long JGBs in September, and unwinding could weigh on the market briefly.
Receiving BoJ meeting dates in OIS could be considered a kind of option trade as hike pricing fades.
geopolitical: Middle East situation deteriorated in March, raising oil prices, with a medium-term upside inflation risk if turmoil persists.
Citi commodity analysts expect the US and Iran to return to the negotiation process.
President Trump raised JPY weakness directly with PM Takaichi at a September 22 summit.
Turmoil in French government bonds (OATs) is spilling over into global rates.

tension_points.bull_case: Hawkish case: inflation is approaching 2%, oil pass-through lifts CPI from autumn, a Fed December hike and yen weakness risk justify continued quarterly hikes to 2%.
tension_points.bear_case: Dovish case: price increases are leveling off, the AI-stock correction and French yield spillover could tighten global conditions and delay Fed and ECB hikes, reducing urgency to hike.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A deepening equity correction or tightening global financial conditions delaying Fed and ECB hikes would slow the hike pace. A weaker yen or persistently high inflation would require further tightening.

theme_stances.key_argument: Price pressures justify continued hikes, with the next in December and a 2% terminal rate.
theme_stances.evidence: we continue to expect the next rate hike to come in December

theme_stances.evidence: the currency policy of the Japanese MoF is clearly becoming more hawkish
